projects.title: PTXForge
projects.sub: GPU kernel compiler and autotuner in C++20
projects.data: Measured on a Tesla T4; MLIR path checked on CPU
projects.lede: An MLIR compiler that lowers a fused GEMM + bias + GELU from linalg to PTX, plus a closed-loop autotuner that reaches 85.6% of cuBLAS on a T4 with the nvcc-built kernel.
projects.problem: Choosing tile sizes and shared-memory layout for a GPU kernel by hand is slow, and a wrong guess can cost several times in throughput. PTXForge searches the configuration space with a cost model, measures every candidate on the GPU, and keeps a trace of each decision.
how: The MLIR passes build against LLVM 19 and lower linalg to PTX in six stages, about 0.2 s, with no CUDA toolkit. The kernel takes four pointers and keeps each thread's 4×4 accumulator in registers.
Four custom passes: epilogue fusion, bank-conflict padding for shared memory, an arith-only tanh/fabs so the kernel needs no libdevice, and removal of the no-op copies bufferization leaves behind.
Tile sizes come from a transform schedule the tuner renders per config, so trying a new config needs no C++ rebuild.

Header-only C++20 tuner: a 3,610-config search space, a roofline cost model (arithmetic intensity, register caps, occupancy, wave quantization) and closed-loop search. Advisors (none, random, rules, knowledge graph, LLM) are validated in C++ before anything runs.

The first T4 run showed the cost model ranks near-optimal configs badly (Spearman ρ = −0.67). The tuner still reached 85.6% of cuBLAS because it keeps the measured best, which is the argument for closed-loop measurement.
projects.caveat: The 85.6% comes from one 40-trial tuning run of the nvcc-built kernel on a Colab T4. The MLIR-generated PTX is checked numerically on the CPU but hasn't been run on a GPU yet, and it doesn't stage tiles in shared memory, so expect it to be well below the tuned kernel. The advisor ablation hasn't been run on hardware.

projects.title: minic
projects.lede: A dependency-free compiler for a small imperative language, going through the same stages as a production compiler.
projects.problem: Built to understand every stage between source text and execution, including the parts textbooks skip: error messages with line numbers, forward jumps, and keeping optimizations from changing behaviour.
how: Hand-written lexer with one character of lookahead; recursive-descent parser building an AST.
Constant folding and dead-branch and dead-loop elimination. Folding shares its arithmetic code with the VM, so both agree on overflow and division.
Forward jumps are resolved by backpatching, the same problem linkers solve with relocations.
Semantic analysis runs before optimization, so removing dead code can never change which programs compile.

projects.title: cuda-gpu-bench
projects.sub: CUDA kernels, benchmarked and read down to the PTX
projects.lede: Hand-written CUDA kernels for vector add, matrix multiply and sum reduction, benchmarked on a T4 and explained instruction by instruction.
projects.problem: Each kernel answers one question a GPU performance engineer asks: how much does shared-memory tiling help, and what does synchronization cost (atomics vs shared-memory tree vs warp shuffles)?
how: Naive and shared-memory tiled matrix multiply, plus three reductions: contended atomics, shared-memory tree and warp shuffle.
Built with nvcc for sm_75 and run on a Tesla T4; every kernel passes its CPU-reference check before it is timed.
Tiling gained 1.5×, not the 16× the load count suggests: the naive kernel's loads already go through the read-only cache. Register tiling is the next step.
A CPU emulator of threads, blocks, shared memory, barriers, atomics and warp shuffles runs the kernel logic on any machine; deliberately broken kernels are all caught.
results: Matmul at N = 2048, tiled vs naive
projects.caveat: Median of 3 runs on one Colab T4. The hand-written matmul is a teaching kernel; it sits at about 15% of cuBLAS.

projects.title: Opinion Lineage System
projects.lede: Estimates organic sentiment from streams full of reposts, paraphrases, coordinated copies and AI rewrites, and corrects published estimates when provenance changes.
projects.problem: Counting every post equally lets amplification pass as opinion. When a source is later found to be a bot network, the published sentiment is already wrong.
how: A calibrated gradient-boosted edge model labels each post as a repost, quote, paraphrase, AI derivative or coordinated copy of an earlier one.
Weights down-rank dependent and synthetic posts so the aggregate reflects independent opinion.
Selective Dependency Rollback turns a provenance revision into an exact update over the affected lineage only, with no model re-runs.
A RAG layer gives each lineage one evidence slot, says how much volume is amplification, and corrects answers in place when a source is retracted.
results: RAG answer error, lineage-aware vs naive

projects.title: RailConflict-PSCL
projects.lede: A collision-risk classifier with two safety layers, tested on a railway graph digital twin with degraded sensor data.
projects.problem: A classifier that is accurate on average can still miss the rare Critical encounters that matter most. The goal was to cut those misses without flooding drivers with false emergencies.
how: Labels are the minimum physical intervention that avoids each conflict, computed from hidden true state.
Mondrian conformal prediction gives per-severity-class bounds on under-classification; the decision is the most severe tier in the set.
An ETCS-style braking shield overrides the model when physics says a stop is needed.
projects.caveat: Results come from a simulated railway network, not field data.

projects.title: TrustDecay-TKG
projects.lede: Forecasts how far each IT asset's trust has decayed since its last audit, then turns forecasts into an audit queue with a guarantee on missed assets.
projects.problem: Audit teams cover a fraction of assets each cycle. Rotation and severity-score rules spend that budget on the wrong assets.
how: Events become time-stamped graph quadruples; features summarise each asset's recent history and neighbourhood.
Delayed-feedback adaptive conformal selection handles audit outcomes that arrive weeks late and holds missed severe assets near a target rate.
Ablations showed the gain comes from temporal features; relational graph features added little in this setting.
projects.caveat: Everything runs on a simulated enterprise; results describe this simulator, not real organisations.

projects.title: VeriCloud
projects.lede: Verifies claims against retrieved evidence while learning which sources to trust, and abstains when evidence is thin.
projects.problem: Coordinated sybil sites can outvote real sources. Verification has to stay accurate when part of the evidence is planted.
how: Hybrid retrieval, a gradient-boosted stance model and Bayesian source-reliability learning are fused into a calibrated verdict.
Monte-Carlo sampling of reliabilities gives a credible interval and a verdict-flip probability.
Claims are split by time, and significance is tested with paired Wilcoxon tests across seeds.
projects.caveat: All numbers come from a synthetic news world with known attackers. They show how the mechanisms behave, not real-world accuracy.

projects.title: Risk-Constrained Emergency Control
projects.lede: Predicts whether a candidate micro-intervention will be protective, harmful, ineffective or inconsistent before it is physically tested.
projects.problem: In emergency control, trying an action to see what happens can make things worse. This screener is the first safety layer before escalation.
how: A four-zone, source-informed generator produces 5,000 labelled records.
Three classifiers are compared with a safety-first selection rule; a gate tuned on out-of-fold training predictions blocks uncertain actions.
A hard protected-zone constraint is applied before the model is ever consulted, and tests pin it at its exact thresholds.
Deployed as a live web console on Vercel; built as a course project on the published patent.
results: Unsafe passed as safe, with the gate

projects.title: Wildfire Prediction and Response
projects.lede: An ensemble with confidence-gated risk levels, resource allocation under scarcity and champion/challenger retraining, behind a Flask dashboard.
projects.problem: Fire services need a risk level they can act on and a way to allocate scarce crews, not just a probability.
how: Trains on the UCI Forest Fires data with the patent disclosure's own experimental setup, and reports cross-validated results instead of the disclosure's projected figures.
Monotonic constraints guarantee that hotter, drier or windier weather can never lower the predicted risk. Before them, a simulated heatwave scored lower than a cool wet day in 11 of 12 months.
Evacuation advisories are drafted automatically but wait for human sign-off, and simulated data can never retrain the model.
projects.caveat: 517 fires from one park. The models beat chance only modestly; the disclosure's 90–95% figures are projections for a future sensor deployment, not results.

projects.title: Mine Tremor Detection
projects.lede: Simulation of distributed sensor nodes that classify vibration on the edge and confirm tremors across several nodes before alerting.
projects.problem: A single vibration sensor raises false alarms from machinery. Multi-node confirmation trades a little latency for far fewer false alerts.
how: Each node (ESP32 + MPU6050 in the design) runs a Random Forest and checks its prediction against physical thresholds.
Streaming detection, latency and firmware fault injection are simulated in three stages.
Pitched to NRDC for grant funding.
projects.caveat: Every result comes from synthetic signals, not hardware or field measurements.

projects.title: agentic-bug-repair
projects.lede: Takes a Java repository with failing tests and tries to produce a verified fix as a pull request, in the style of SWE-agent systems but small enough to read in a sitting.
projects.problem: A failing build usually needs a person to find the faulty method and try fixes by hand. The agent automates that loop and only publishes a diff that passes every test on a clean checkout.
how: The JDK compiler API parses the repository into a code graph with call, import, inheritance and field-write edges.
Fault localization combines test failures, the graph and text retrieval to rank suspect methods.
Candidate diffs run in an isolated sandbox; failures are fed back for up to three correction rounds.
A GitHub webhook can trigger runs, and a dashboard shows the state machine, the diff and telemetry. State-changing calls require same-origin JSON on a loopback host.
results: Bug in top 3 suspects, graph vs text
Bug ranked first, graph vs text
projects.caveat: With 17 bugs, the localization differences are not statistically significant. The model-backed repair path has only been tested against a stub API, the Docker sandbox has not been run, and no real GitHub pull request has been opened. These numbers are not comparable to SWE-bench scores.

projects.title: mini-kv-store
projects.lede: A small storage engine built the way production LSM stores are, and tested by crashing it on purpose.
projects.problem: A key-value store is only useful if a crash at any moment leaves it recoverable with no acknowledged write lost.
how: The write-ahead log carries checksums and truncates a torn tail on recovery.
SSTables have sparse indexes and Bloom filters; compaction is a k-way merge, and the manifest is swapped atomically.
Tests inject a crash at every flush and compaction step and check that recovery is correct.
results: at every flush and compaction step

projects.title: system-design-primitives
projects.lede: The building blocks that system-design interviews ask about, implemented and tested instead of drawn on a whiteboard.
projects.problem: Knowing that an LRU cache or a token bucket exists is different from getting its edge cases right.
how: LRU and LFU caches, token-bucket and sliding-window rate limiters, consistent hashing and a Bloom filter.
Each is checked against a reference implementation and covered by tests for its edge cases.

projects.title: dsa-patterns
projects.sub: Interview patterns, tested against brute force
projects.lede: Algorithm patterns organised by how to recognise the problem, each checked against a brute-force solution.
projects.problem: Pattern libraries often contain subtle bugs because they are only tested on a few hand-picked examples.
how: 13 classes of patterns, organised by the clue in the problem statement that points to them.
Every solution is compared with a brute force on thousands of random inputs.
Planted bugs were used to check that the tests have teeth: 9 of 11 were caught, and the other 2 behave identically to the original.

projects.title: Healthcare Appointment Manager
projects.lede: A REST backend for patients, doctors and admins where two people can never book the same slot and no notification is silently lost.
projects.problem: Booking systems fail at the edges: two requests for one slot, a doctor's leave added after bookings exist, an email provider that times out.
how: PostgreSQL exclusion constraints and 5-minute slot holds prevent double-booking; a concurrent booking gets a clear conflict error.
Leave creation and booking take the same row lock, so they can't race.
A transactional outbox with retries and a dead-letter queue makes notifications reliable.
LLM visit summaries are schema-validated, can't invent a drug the doctor didn't prescribe, and fall back to a deterministic template when the model fails.
projects.caveat: This repository holds the backend; the React portals are not included.

projects.title: Inventory Management System
projects.sub: Secure REST API with an audit trail
projects.lede: A small inventory service with real security controls and a tamper-evident audit log.
projects.problem: Stock records are only useful if you can prove nobody quietly edited them.
how: PBKDF2 password hashing, role-based access and signed tokens.
Every change is appended to a hash-chained audit log that can be verified end to end.
Sensor telemetry is reconciled against book stock; an optional retrieval layer answers questions with an injection-aware prompt.

projects.title: PDF-to-Audio Generator
projects.lede: Upload a text-based PDF and get a narration back, with interchangeable speech backends.
projects.problem: Long documents hit speech-API limits and flaky networks; the service has to chunk, retry and report progress.
how: Cleans PDF text for speech: re-flows wrapped lines, re-joins hyphenated words, drops page numbers, running headers and citation markers.
Packs whole sentences into chunks under Google's 5,000-byte limit, counted in bytes so Hindi and Tamil text doesn't overflow.
Google Cloud Text-to-Speech, gTTS or offline eSpeak behind one interface; background jobs with progress, cancel, cache and expiry.
